STRCOMMENT
This is a comment. Comments in structure files (*.str) start with // . All text from here to newline will be ignored, so it may be used for comments.
aboutStruc:
*.str files describe the crystal structures as to be refined. In general, every *.str file contains two parts: (i) describing the lattice (spacegroup, lattice parameters) and real structure (line widths etc.) and (ii) describing the atomic settings for this structure. The latter starts with the first occurrence of the E= assignment in the file. If no atomic positions are given and FMult is not in use, a LeBail-Fit (refinement of independent peak intensities) will be done.
Comments start with // as a single item.
LatticeDefinition: RealStructure: IdealStructure: molecules: GeneralCondition= PARAM= UNIT= GOAL FMult= my my[i] density density[i]
part1
GeneralCondition=
The term as assigned to GeneralCondition should depend from h k l. Enables the deselection of peaks from the pattern. Example:
GeneralCondition=and(eq(h,0),eq(k,0),eq(abs(l),2)
will select the 002 reflection only, for hexagonal lattice. Of course, such a selection must select/deselect all equivalent reflections in an equal manner.
May depend from iref, so different conditions for different subphases may be used.
aboutStruc: RefMult=
PARAM=
Each structure or real structure variable may be declared as a parameter to be refined by typing
PARAM=variable_lowerlimit^upperlimit
upperlimit and lowerlimit are hard limits, the parameter value is not allowed to leave that interval during refinement.
aboutStruc:
part1
my=
Using my= you may set a user defined linear attenuation coefficient of the phase. You may use the variables my[i].
Attention: In difference to the usual conventions, my has the unit µm-1.
aboutStruc: my[i] RefMult= FMult=
part1
my
my will be preset to the linear attenuation coefficient. Attention: In difference to the usual conventions, my has the unit µm-1. May be used for the Brindley correction as follows:
GOAL:xxx=GEWICHT*exp(my*d*3/4)
where xxx is the name of the phase and d is its grain size.
In the case RefMult>1, my refers to the linear attenuation coefficient of the first subphase iref=1.
In cases you use other wavelengths than the usual (Co, Cr, Cu, Fe) for which no file *.mdr exist, my will be set to zero. This is especially the case when using SYNCHROTRON= or LAMDA= with an numeric value in the *.sav file for this BGMN run.
aboutStruc: GEWICHT GOAL
part1
my[i]
In case FMult>0, my[i] will be set to the linear attenuation coefficient as caused by all atomic positions which contribute to the calculation of F[i]. Otherwise, my[i] will be preset to the linear attenuation coefficient of the ith Subphase, which may useful in cases RefMult>1. Attention: In difference to the usual conventions, my has the unit µm-1.

part1

LatticeDefinition:
The lattice must be defined for every run of BGMN. Therefore
SpacegroupNo= or HermannMauguin must be given. In addition, the lattice constants A B C ALPHA BETA GAMMA must be set corresponding to the given lattice. For example, a cubic lattice needs only for setting of A. It is favourable to set meaningful limits for the lattice parameters like
PARAM=A=0.325_0.324^0.326

UNIT=
On default, the unit of all values in lattice and reciprocal lattice is Nanometer.
UNIT=NM
If set to
UNIT=ANGSTROEM
all lengths in space and reciprocal space are given in Angstroem: A B C ALPHA BETA GAMMA sk DELTAsk TDS B1 B2
The exception is the linear attenuation coefficient µ, which is always given in 1/µm.

RealStructure:
There are several ways to define the peak broadening model. In every case, the defined peak profile is only the sample contribution P of the folding product Lambda*G*P, where
Lambda is the wavelenth distribution = spectrum of the X-rays. (e.g. the CuKalpha doublet) Gis the geometry function as computed by GEOMET/VERZERR and MAKEGEQ.

part1
RP=
Defines the type of peak shape assumed for P (sample broadening) in the folding LAMBDA*G*P. Possible values are
2Only a delta-peak will be used for P. Therefore, all assignments to B1 and B2 will be ignored. 3A Lorentzian with width parameter B1/B1[i] will be used for P. This model describes pure crystallite size caused line broadening. 4 (default value) To combine crystallite size and micro strain brodening effects, the Lorentzian will be folded with a squared Lorentzian with width parameter B2 or B2[i]. In normal, B2 will not be set directly, it defaults to
B2=k1*sqr(B1)+k2*sqr(sk)

width of the lorentzian part of P in 1/nm, assuming a crystallite size caused line broadening. The special setting

GEWICHT
GEWICHT is the scale factor while refining multiphase specimens. It is proportional directly to the weight fraction, no additional calculation of ZMV is necessary. The simplest way is typing
PARAM=GEWICHT=0_0
There are different ways in using this key. For example
GEWICHT=SPHAR6
defines a series of symmetrized spherical harmonics of 6th order including the scale factor. That means, for every line h k l a new value for GEWICHT will be computed following these spherical harmonics.
For getting the mean weight proportional scale factor (as needed for quantitative analysis) just type
GOAL:phaseid=GEWICHT
and the mean value of the spherical harmonic will be assigned to phaseid. In following, phaseid is exported and may be used in GOALS inside the *.sav file for the calculation of relative phase abundances. The predefined value of GEWICHT is corrected for phase density as to the value as predefined for the value density, which is that of the first suphase in cases RefMult>1. Therefore the results refers directly to the weight content of the phase.
For the Brindley correction, see my.

If not given (which should be in normal), BGMN uses an advanced value depending from the Laue Group of the phase.

ANISO
ANISO is a shortcut for the four special cases:
B1=ANISO means B1=ANISOLIN
k2=ANISO means k2=ANISOSQR
GEWICHT=ANISO means GEWICHT=ANISOQR
TDS=ANISO means TDS=ANISOQR
The use of ANISO for any other variable is faulty!
RealStructure: ANISOLIN ANISOSQR ANISOLIMIT= ANISO4 ANISO4LIMIT=
part1
ANISOSQR
ANISOSQR may be assigned to real structure variable. While computing the pattern, for each peak a quadratic form of the normalized Laue indices vector over a positive definite matrix will be refined and assigned to the variable. This means, in maximum 6 parameters have to be calculated. The matrix fulfills automatically the symmetry conditions of the point group. This is useful for anisotropic strain (k2) broadening as well as for anisotropic temperature factors (TDS).
RealStructure: k2= TDS= ANISOLIN ANISOLIMIT= ANISO4 ANISO4LIMIT=
part1
ANISOLIN
ANISOLINmay be assigned to real structure variables. While computing the pattern, for each peak a quadratic form of the normalized Laue indices vector over a positive definite matrix will be refined and its square root will be assigned to the variable. This means, in maximum 6 parameters have to be calculated. The matrix fulfills automatically the symmetry conditions of the point group. This is useful for anisotropic size (B1). factors.
RealStructure: B1= ANISOSQR ANISOLIMIT= ANISO4 ANISO4LIMIT=
part1
ANISOLIMIT=
BGMN tries a first run, whereby isotropic replacements to ANISOLIN and ANISOSQR are assumed. Afterwards the resulting parameter value will be checked for significance. ANISOLIMIT sets this significance limit. If this significance test fails, an isotropic model for the parameter will be choosen instead of ANISO. If not given (which should be in normal), BGMN uses an advanced value depending from the Laue Group of the phase.
RealStructure: ANISOLIN ANISOSQR ANISO4 ANISO4LIMIT=
part1
ANISO4
ANISO4 may be assigned to any real structure variable. While computing the pattern, for each peak the full (4x) product of the normalized Laue indices over a positive definite tensor of 4th stage will be refined. This means, in general 15 parameters have to be calculated. The tensor fulfills automatically the symmetry conditions of the point group.
ANISO4 was designed for k2 and k2[i].
RealStructure: ANISOSQR ANISOLIN ANISOLIMIT= ANISO4LIMIT= k2= k2[i]=
part1
ANISO4LIMIT=
BGMN tries a first run, whereby an isotropic replacements to ANISO4 will be assumed. Afterwards the resulting parameter value will be checked for significance. ANISO4LIMIT sets this significance limit. If this significance test fails, the ANISOSQR model for the parameter will be choosen instead of ANISO4. If not given (which should be in normal), BGMN uses an advanced value depending from the Laue Group of the phase.
RealStructure: ANISOLIN ANISOSQR ANISOLIMIT= ANISOSQR ANISO4
part1

molecules:
The molecules feature will be switched on by assigning a positive value to
THEORY=
Using set(a,x,y,z)/setgitter(a,x,y,z), one may define molecules. Molecules are no rigid bodies, their internal angles and molecular distances may be changed by T(a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma,e...) or D(a,b,chi,e...). The static interaction energy between molecules may be set by WW(a,m,b,n,liste...). Internal bondings may be defined by Bondings= and BondLevel=. Atoms which are "bonded" are not used while executing the WW(a,m,b,n,liste...) functions.
In general, the molecules extension uses arrays to hold the atom positions. Thereby, an atomic position descriptor (e.g. N6) must be a non-indexed variable. Looking at this example N6, BGMN uses N6[1], N6[2] and N6[3] for the cartesian coordinate description.

cross(a,b,c,x)
The first three arguments of cross(a,b,c,x) define atomic positions. cross sets the 4th as the cross product of the both distance vectors a-b and b-c starting on c. So, c-x will be orthogonal to a-b and b-c. If a,b,c are collinear, x coincides with b.

diffvec(a,b,c) sets the third vector as the difference vector between the first an the second atomic position.

normvec(a,b) normalizes the three cartesian coordinates as given by a[1]...a[3], the result will be set to b[1]...b[3]. The resulting vector b has the same direction as a, but the length 1 (unit vector in direction of a)

angle(a,b...) has three definitions depending on the parameter count:
with 2 arguments: returns the angle between both vectors in degree with 3 arguments: returns the angle enclosed between the atomic positions a-b-c with 4 arguments: returns the torsion angle between the 4 atomic positions a-b-c-d

Theory=
Theory defaults to zero. By setting to a positive value, the force field extensions
WW(a,m,b,n,liste...), WWalt(a,m,b,n,liste...)
Straf(x)
will be added to the refinemnt. By this way, a combined minimum for both the measured pattern and the force field will be computed.
The numerical value of the force field extension will be multiplied with the value assigned to Theory during refinement.
molecules: WW(a,m,b,n,liste...) WWalt(a,m,b,n,liste...) Straf(x)
part1
cpXYZ(a,b...)
After having defined the molecule with set(a,x,y,z) (or setgitter(a,x,y,z)), cpXYZ(a,b...) generates copies with identic co-ordinates. cpXYZ must be called with even parameter count. Within each pair of parameters, the co-ordinates of the left one are copied to the right-one. The right-one parameter may be a comma-separated list in brackets:
cpXYZ(a,(b,c,d))
By this way, multiple copies are generated from one source.

F(phi...)
F calculated dynamically a structure factor. The atomic positions in part 2 of the structure file will be calculated only once prior to all hkl calculations. In contrast, F will be calculated every time it will be called. In special, F may be used within the standard function cintegral for calculation of arbitrary random distribution of molecules. Example:
FMult=1 F=cat(fmittelbetrag==cintegral(fi,F(psi, D2(r1,r2,rot,EOZ1,eoz1,EOZ2,eoz2,EOZ3,eoz3,EOZ4,eoz4,EOZ5,eoz5,EOZ6,eoz6), E=NA+1(pCA),Wyckoff=c,XYZ(ECA),TDS==tdsint, E=O-2(pOZ),Wyckoff=c,XYZ(eoz1),TDS==tdsH2O, E=O-2(pOZ),Wyckoff=c,XYZ(eoz2),TDS==tdsH2O, E=O-2(pOZ),Wyckoff=c,XYZ(eoz3),TDS==tdsH2O, E=O-2(pOZ),Wyckoff=c,XYZ(eoz4),TDS==tdsH2O, E=O-2(pOZ),Wyckoff=c,XYZ(eoz5),TDS==tdsH2O, E=O-2(pOZ),Wyckoff=c,XYZ(eoz6),TDS==tdsH2O), psi,rot,0,120)/120, sqrt(sqr(F[1]*cos(pi*phi[1]/180)+fmittelbetrag*cos(pi*fi/180))+ sqr(F[1]*sin(pi*phi[1]/180)+fmittelbetrag*sin(pi*fi/180))))
will calculate the strucure factor including a rotating octahedron.

WW(a,m,b,n,liste...)
WW(a,m,b,n,liste...) defines nonbonding or bonding interactions (likehydrogen bonds) using list of atomic positions descriptors as define by set/setgitter an moved around by using the T(a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma,e...) and D(a,b,chi,e...) functions.In every case, the bonding/nonbonding energy will be
a*rm+b*rn
May be used with 5 or 6 parameters. Uses one or two lists of atomic descriptors, for example
WW(a,m,b,n,(C1,C2,C3)) declares all force fields between C1,C2 und C3, which are 3:
C1-C2, C1-C3 and C2-C3 WW(a,m,b,n,(C1,C2),(N1,N2)) declares all force fieldsbetween both lists, which ar 4:
C1-N1, C1-N2, C2-N1 anc C2-N2
for partially occupied settings, the product of both settings (always 0<=p1*p2<=1 will be multiplied to the force field penalty.
In every case, Bondings and BondLevel may exclude atomic pairings from the penalty function.

part1
GOAL
There are two kinds of GOAL:
direct: GOAL=A/C
indirect: GOAL:outer=A/C
The difference: The direct GOAL will be reported with errors in the result file *.lst. The indirect GOAL assignes the result of an expression to a helper variable, which then can be used in an outer environment.
For example: We assume 2 phase files named a.str and b.str.
File a.str contains the item GOAL:a=GEWICHT
File b.str contains the item GOAL:b=GEWICHT
Then, in the outer *.sav file, one may set the items
GOAL[1]=a/(a+b) GOAL[2]=b/(a+b)
which will give the total weight fractions of both phases and their random errors.

integral(y,x,xu,xo...)
integral(y,x,xu,xo) calculates a numeric integral. integrand will be y, the integral will be carried out over x between xu and xo. For minmization of the numeric effort, an adaptive 7-point-formula will be used. The precision of the numeric integration may be set as a fifth parameter, default is 1E-13 (which will, for the fast converging 7-point formula, reach a precision near to 1E-15). Example:
integral(sin(x),x,0,acos(0))
will calculate 1.0.

cintegral(phi,yabs,yphase,x,xu,xo...)
cintegral(phy,yabs,yphase,x,xu,xo) calculates a complex numeric integral. The absolute value of the integrand will be yabs, its complex phase angle yphase. The integral will be carried out over x between xu and xo. For minmization of the numeric effort, an adaptive 7-point-formula will be used. The precision of the numeric integration may be set as a fifth parameter, default is 1E-13 (which will, for the fast converging 7-point formula, reach a precision near to 1E-15). cintegral returns the absolute value of the integral, its phase angle will be set to the variable given at first position (phi). Example:
cintegral(phi,1,90*x/acos(0),x,0,acos(0))
will calculate the square root of 2, phi will be set to 45.

gauss(A,x,b,eps,n)
gauss(A,x,b,eps,n) is a high-level standard functions for solving linear equation systems. A,x,b are placeholder for arrays, therefore only non-indexed names are allowed. gauss solves the inhomogen linear equation system
Ax=b
where A is the matrix A[1,1]...A[n,n], b is the right side b[1]...b[n] and x is the unknown solution x[1]...x[n]. eps is a limit for the pivot element, if any pivot element is smaller than eps the equation leaves unsolved and zero (false) will be returned. If the equation system has been solved and x[1]...x[n] hold the solution, 1 (true) will be returned.

A function call is a name followed by a list of actual parameters in brackets () separated by commas. There are some predefined functions, in general. In addition, functions may be defined in the input file. Functions calls may become recursive. Only the actual stack depth of the BGMN program may become a run time problem for deeply nested function calls.

Arrays are variable names followed by a list of indices separated by commas, in brackets []. Indices may be arbitrary expressions.
* *(x...) expression:
*
Arbitrary variables may be defined by assigning a value. The first character of the name must be a letter, the following characters may be letters or decimal digits. This rule is also valid for the names of arrays and functions. Any variable may, in general, hold one of two types of values: either a double number or a string value. An expression is a special case of a string value. All programs use some variable names for program control. In addition, some variables may be predefined in special cases/positions by the program.

assignment:
Assignments are variable names (maybe indexed) followed by one ore more assignment characters = and a string. In special, the string may be a variable or an expression. In general, a single = assigns the string value of the right hand side to the left hand variable. Other behaviour may be controlled by multiple =. Some examples:
A=1
B=A
C=B
D==C
E===C
F====C
G=====C
H==(C) I==C+B
K==1
After doing the above assignments from top to bottom,
A holds the string 1
B holds the string A
C holds the string B
D holds the string B
E holds the string A
F holds the string 1
G holds the double value 1.0
H holds the double value 1.0
I holds the double value 2.0
K holds the double value 1.0
